report_name: Amplifon Reports Data Breach Months After Initial Intrusion

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: An unauthorized party exfiltrated files from Amplifon's systems between January 18 and February 8, 2026. The nature of the exfiltrated data, containing personal information, was not confirmed until October 2026.

campaigns.name: Amplifon Data Breach January-February 2026
campaigns.description: An unauthorized party gained access to Amplifon's systems for approximately three weeks between January and February 2026, exfiltrating files containing personal and financial information. The breach was detected in February but the impact on personal data was not confirmed until October.

identities.name: Amplifon (USA), Inc.
identities.description: A global provider of hearing care services and products that suffered a data breach where an unauthorized party accessed its network and exfiltrated files containing personal information, including Social Security numbers and financial data.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Upload to Cloud Storage
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Upload to Cloud Storage
id: 9b8e1f2d-3c4a-4b5c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: Detects unusually large data uploads to common cloud storage providers, which could indicate data exfiltration as suggested in the Amplifon data breach report.
references:
  - https://www.classaction.org/data-breach-lawsuits/amplifon-november-2026
author: cyber.netsecio.io
date: 2026-11-07
tags:
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate large file transfers to corporate or personal cloud storage.
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_domains:
    cs-host|endswith:
      - '.dropbox.com'
      - '.drive.google.com'
      - '.sharepoint.com'
      - '.onedrive.live.com'
      - '.box.com'
      - '.mega.nz'
  selection_size:
    sc-bytes|gt: 10000000
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects unusually large data uploads (over 10MB) to common cloud storage providers. This pattern was suggested as a potential data exfiltration method in the Amplifon breach.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Large Data Upload to Cloud Storage
